name: Lesbian feminism
summary: Lesbian feminism is the strand of radical feminism, formed around 1970 in the Radicalesbians and the Furies, that treats heterosexuality as the institution that ties each woman to a man and holds male supremacy in place, and calls women to put women first. It rejects fixed sex roles, marriage and the nuclear family, condemns pornography as woman-hating, and splits over separatism, over whether sex itself is constructed, and over the sex wars. Its writers range from separatists to socialists such as the Combahee women, who rejected separatism.
scope: The radical lesbian-feminist writing of the 1970s and early 1980s: the Radicalesbians (1970), the Furies collective (Bunch, Brown, Small, Reid), Rich on compulsory heterosexuality, Frye, Wittig, the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group, and Bunch's later international lesbian rights work, with Combahee as the Black socialist strand that dissented on separatism. Positions of feminism in general, the gay movement, queer theory or the wider left are not borrowed; its own texts say little on economics, government and world affairs, so those answers are null.

keyFigures.name: Adrienne Rich
keyFigures.role: Poet and theorist whose 'compulsory heterosexuality' and 'lesbian existence' essay is a founding text.

keyFigures.name: Charlotte Bunch
keyFigures.role: Furies member and theorist of lesbian feminism as the basis of women's liberation, later an international lesbian-rights organiser.

keyFigures.name: Monique Wittig
keyFigures.role: Materialist lesbian-feminist theorist of sex as a political category.

sources.author: Radicalesbians
sources.usedFor: The 1970 manifesto: sex roles, male supremacy, heterosexual structure, marriage, women-identification.

sources.title: Lesbians in Revolt (The Furies, January 1972)
sources.author: Charlotte Bunch
sources.usedFor: Lesbianism as political choice, sexism as root oppression, family, work, seizing power, separate movement.

sources.title: The Shape of Things to Come (The Furies, in Women: A Journal of Liberation)
sources.author: Rita Mae Brown
sources.usedFor: Heterosexuality as the base of male supremacy, race and class as offshoots, practical programme (work projects, consciousness-raising, media, ideology, a party).

sources.title: Lesbians and the Class Position of Women (speech for The Furies)
sources.author: Margaret Small
sources.usedFor: Wives' unpaid domestic labour as slavery, Marxism's blind spot on women, heterosexual ideology, the lesbian's position.

sources.title: Coming Out in the Women's Movement (The Furies)
sources.author: Coletta Reid
sources.usedFor: Marriage, family, sex roles and job discrimination as constructs of male supremacy; lesbians want self-determination and a share in governing.

sources.title: The Normative Status of Heterosexuality (Purple September Staff, reprinted in the Furies collection)
sources.author: Purple September (Dutch lesbian feminists)
sources.usedFor: Heterosexuality as a norm that perpetuates the power relation between the sexes.

sources.title: Compulsory Heterosexuality and Lesbian Existence (Signs, 1980)
sources.author: Adrienne Rich
sources.usedFor: Heterosexuality as a political institution; the catalogue of male power over women (marriage, unpaid labour, pornography, purdah, abortion control, sterilization).

sources.title: Political Lesbianism: The Case Against Heterosexuality (1979), in Love Your Enemy? (Onlywomen Press, 1981)
sources.author: Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group
sources.usedFor: The heterosexual couple as the unit of male supremacy; abandoning heterosexuality; the group's afterword on separatism and its limits.

sources.title: Lesbian Feminism and the Gay Rights Movement: Another View of Male Supremacy, Another Separatism (in The Politics of Reality)
sources.author: Marilyn Frye
sources.usedFor: Male citizenship presumption, pornography as woman-hating, why lesbian feminists do not see gay rights as a shared cause.

sources.title: The Straight Mind and Other Essays
sources.author: Monique Wittig
sources.usedFor: Sex as a political category, the marriage contract, 'women' as a class to be abolished, against natural-difference doctrines.

sources.title: The Combahee River Collective Statement (1977)
sources.author: Combahee River Collective
sources.usedFor: The Black lesbian socialist strand: rejects separatism and biological determinism; used for the documented split on separatism and the class analysis.

sources.title: Lesbians Travel the Roads of Feminism Globally (Center for Women's Global Leadership, 2000)
sources.author: Charlotte Bunch and Claudia Hinojosa
sources.usedFor: Lesbian rights as human rights; 1977 Houston plank, UN conferences and international lesbian networking.

sources.title: Lesbian Feminism (Encyclopedia of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender History in America)
sources.author: Stephanie Gilmore and Anne Collinson, via Encyclopedia.com
sources.usedFor: Scholarly overview: origins, separatism, marriage and family, sex wars, trans exclusion disputes, race and class conflicts.

sources.author: Carisa R. Showden

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Radicalesbians call society one dominated by male supremacy that casts women as a serving caste, and Bunch and Rich describe male power over women as the base of the whole social order.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The manifesto treats sex roles as a male-supremacist construct (being feminine and being a whole person are irreconcilable), and Reid and Wittig likewise treat the 'natural' roles of women and sex difference as social products.

traditional-family.rationale: Bunch says the lesbian rejects the nuclear family as the basic unit of capitalist production and consumption, and Reid lists the family and housewifery among the constructs men built on women's reproductive role.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Radicalesbians hold that fixed sex roles dehumanize women and are the basis of male supremacy; the movement aims to end them.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Lesbian feminists organised for lesbian rights as part of women's rights and human rights, including securing the 'sexual preference' plank at Houston in 1977, and Frye treats laws that sanction civil injury to lesbians and gay men as an injustice.

women-suffrage.rationale: Frye holds that the presumption of male citizenship (rights to property, movement and so on) is basic to male-supremacist society, and she cites the 72 years it took to win the vote as evidence of it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Frye lists ownership and disposition of property among the rights presumed male under the 'presumption of male citizenship' that feminism challenges.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The sources condemn a husband's authority but reject marriage itself; they state no position on how spouses should share authority.

women-must-cover.rationale: Rich lists purdah, the veil and feminine dress codes among the means by which men confine women, so a law compelling women to cover themselves is such a means.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Lesbian feminists advocated overthrowing marriage as an institution oppressive to women: Reid calls marriage legalized prostitution, Wittig treats the marriage contract as the appropriation of women's labour and persons, and the encyclopedia reports many wanting it overthrown.

paid-care-work.rationale: The Furies and Wittig texts analyse unpaid domestic labour but state no position on paying for care work.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Bunch calls economics a crucial part of women's oppression, and says lesbians' refusal of unpaid housework and the nuclear family strains capitalism, though she holds the analysis is incomplete and that male supremacy is the root.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bunch writes that oppressed people end oppression only by seizing power, and Brown calls for revolt against male supremacy and for a party to lead the struggle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Small argues that heterosexual ideology sets the limits of what people can perceive, and Wittig that 'natural' sex difference is a social opposition disguised as nature by the dominant thought.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rich names male control of abortion, contraception and childbirth, with enforced sterilization, among the means by which men exploit women's labour, and Reid says lesbians want self-determination over their bodies and children.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Rich and Frye condemn pornography as woman-hating and Rich calls it pernicious, but the encyclopedia reports that many lesbian feminists took the sex-positive side of the sex wars and opposed the anti-pornography camp, so adherents split on legal restriction.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Wittig holds that sex itself is a political category that must be abolished, while Wittig herself reports lesbians who take sex difference to be natural (men biologically inferior), and Combahee rejects biological determinism: strands split on whether sex is constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Wittig treats 'woman' as an imaginary formation to be destroyed, while Bunch and the Leeds group build politics on women as a sex class set against men, so the strands differ.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Combahee holds that racial, sexual, heterosexual and class oppression interlock and must be fought together, while the Furies call sexism the root and race and class its offshoots to be fought through the war on male supremacy.

missingStatements.text: Heterosexuality is a political institution that keeps women subordinate to men, not simply a natural orientation.
missingStatements.rationale: Rich, the Leeds group and the Furies all state it as the movement's central thesis.
missingStatements.declined: Theory wording a general reader would need explained.

missingStatements.text: Women should organise politically in groups that exclude men.
missingStatements.rationale: The Furies, Leeds and Frye argue for women-only and separate organising, while Combahee rejects separatism as a strategy.

missingStatements.text: Feminists should end sexual and emotional relationships with men as a political act.
missingStatements.rationale: Bunch, Brown and the Leeds group argue that feminists should give up relationships with men; Reid and others describe it as an option, and Combahee rejects the separatist version.
missingStatements.declined: A personal choice, not a political position most people could answer.

notes: Searched every theme in the available full texts (Radicalesbians, five Furies essays, Rich, Leeds, Frye, Wittig, Combahee, Bunch and Hinojosa, two reference entries): economy, government, world, ecology, technology and globalism are almost silent, so most answers are null. Strands differ on separatism (Combahee against), on whether sex is constructed (Wittig against natural-difference lesbians), and on pornography (anti-pornography against sex-positive lesbian feminists). Not reachable: Jeffreys's The Lesbian Heresy, Johnston's Lesbian Nation, Atkinson's Amazon Odyssey, Hoagland's Lesbian Ethics, the Furies newsletter (archive.org lending, 401 or no text) and Daly's books, so Daly's positions on ecology, religion and the nature of women are not recorded.
